liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Saint of Circumstance/** (1 review, 1 other source): Saint of Circumstance is cut off at its end; All circulating sources have a cut at the end of Saint of Circumstance, with no patch available [2][13]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review, 1 other source): Eyes has an odd tempo but features lovely playing from Jerry; A short stretch of Eyes Of The World, around 13:03 to 13:17, is supplied from another source [4][9]
- **U.S. Blues** (2 reviews): John Belushi sings on the U.S. Blues encore; John Belushi appeared on stage in the encore, singing backup on U.S. Blues [10][14]
- **Promised Land** (1 review): Bob forgets words in Promised Land [15]
- **Far From Me** (1 review): Far From Me is a shaky, lightweight performance, with Brent missing an entrance at one point [15]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Tennessee Jed is very short, with Jerry cutting the middle jam section short to end the song [13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Jerry's playing on Scarlet Begonias is called the most unforgettable of the night, despite mistakes elsewhere [11]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Jerry's solo in Estimated Prophet is judged cheesy and meandering [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-03-30.mtx.motb.96455.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 170 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1980-03-30.fob.glassberg.motb-0082.96015.flac24**: source not stated; 20 songs; 168 min [2]
- **gd1980-03-30.sbd.miller.92666.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 148 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [4]
- **gd80-03-30.sbd.miller.27752.sbeok.flacf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 151 min; rated 3.56/5 by 9 [5]. Said about its sound: Recording is clear, though the volume level is low [7]
- **gd80-03-30.glassberg.barbella.4740.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 3.62/5 by 13 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound quality good [13]

## Around the show

- Small theater of about 1500 seats, tickets hard to get, and the crowd was wild from the opening Alabama Getaway [11]
- In U.S. Blues, John Belushi contributes vocals and does cartwheels [4]
- John Belushi joined the band on vocals and did cartwheels [5]
- Tickets were harder to get than for the Radio City shows six months later [11]
- Feel Like a Stranger was first played the next night, 3/31, not at this show [15]
- Reviewer rates the Estimated Prophet from Las Vegas 83 far above this one [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-03-30.mtx.motb.96455.flac16**: transferred by Derek McCabe; source: MTX: AUD(96014) and SBD(92666) [1]
- **gd1980-03-30.fob.glassberg.motb-0082.96015.flac24**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Adam Egert and Derek McCabe; source: 2 x Nakamichi CM700 => Sony TC-D5M >> MAC [2]. Also: Source is a Glassberg FOB tape in a 24-bit FLAC transfer, described as a well-edited recording [2]
- **gd1980-03-30.sbd.miller.92666.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat (44.1k) [4]. Also: Chain is Nakamichi 700 to cassette master to DAT to CD; this is a remaster of shnid 27752, pitch-corrected [4]
- **gd80-03-30.sbd.miller.27752.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [5]
- **gd80-03-30.glassberg.barbella.4740.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry G.; source: Audience: Nakamichi 700's [6]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Capitol Theatre - March 30, 1980](https://www.dead.net/show/march-30-1980) [20]
